params.prompt: Production game sprite atlas for the existing cozy RollerCoaster Tycoon inspired isometric pixel-art game. Match references' 2:1 diamond projection, camera 30 degrees down, orthographic, warm soft upper-left light, clear miniature silhouettes, crisp intentionally stepped pixel clusters and restrained palette. Not a rendered voxel scene, not smooth vector icons, not photorealistic. Every object isolated on perfectly solid flat pure MAGENTA #FF00FF chroma-key background, no magenta anywhere on subjects, no alpha/checkerboard simulation, absolutely NO ground plane, contact or cast shadows, grass, landscape, labels, numbers, text, borders, or cell dividers. Spacious empty gutters and margins, no object touches or crosses its cell. Objects fully visible, no cut-off details. Exactly TWELVE sprites in a perfectly aligned FOUR-COLUMN by THREE-ROW grid. Each row shows one same individual in four genuinely different isometric orientations, not four side profiles. Columns left to right: 1 SE head points toward lower-right of image with face visible; 2 SW head points lower-left with face visible; 3 NW head points upper-left, rear/rump closest viewer and face mostly concealed; 4 NE head points upper-right, rear/rump closest viewer and face mostly concealed. Row 1: African elephant, massive broad gray body, four thick legs, large fan ears, long downcurved trunk and small ivory tusks, no saddle. Row 2: male lion, long low ochre-gold quadruped body, rich brown mane around head, long curved tail with dark tuft, four paws, no cartoon upright pose. Row 3: giant panda, distinct rounded stocky quadruped white body with black shoulder band, four black legs, black ears and eye patches, no bamboo prop. Keep the SAME individual, body proportions and source scale within each row; all animals standing naturally on a shared ground contact near the bottom of each cell. Elephant visibly largest, lion elongated medium, panda short and round. Anatomy readable at logical sprite sizes elephant48x40, lion40x32, panda32x32 after reduction. Use broad recognizable markings, avoid fine texture. Four distinct facing directions are essential; no side-only view substituted for rear three-quarter views.

processing: OpenArt originals only. Technical chroma key including dark magenta spill (r>g+24,b>g+24,r+b>90) and gutter-aware extraction; one source scale per animal species; measured ground-plane anchors for buildings; nearest-neighbor logical normalization and exact4x files. Bumper SE is a horizontal mirror of genuine SW. Front layers are alpha-only selections of existing pixels, never repainted.
limits: Animals have one pose per direction; use runtime translation, subtle bob and tilt, not a multi-frame walk.
Bumper car has front SE/SW views only; SE mirrors SW and therefore also mirrors baked lighting.
Balloonride is a complete static preview. Animate individual balloon-gondola sprites around a procedural base/arms; do not simultaneously draw complete preview.
Pavilion is one fixed southeast view. Draw complete pavilion, moving cars/riders, then bumper-pavilion-front for roof/post occlusion.
Buildings use measured ground-plane centers, not bottommost opaque pixels. Apply SpriteSpec anchors without retrimming.
Only architectural sprites are provided for playground; interactive children/3D geometry remain runtime work.
